done_when: When close reports Ready and one or more other items are also Ready, its Next line names one 'forge land <this> <others>' command (forge merge stays for a single Ready item), and the skill has a short 'Keep CI fast' section: land Ready items together, do not rerun close while checks are queued, do not merge main by hand right before a merge; new and existing repos get it on upgrade and forge sync

known.title: Not done: Close names a single merge when its report hides another Ready item
Functional: Exclude the owner-held merge-enable fix from close's batch
Scale: Avoid rebuilding the full next report after every successful close

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a repo runs tests locally while an unrelated, non-required GitHub check is red. Close skips the CI wait and reports the item Ready, but `nextstep.py:1059` and `nextstep.py:897` treat that check as a failure and omit the item from the batch, so this line falls back to `forge merge` despite another Ready item. A cached red result after a successful rerun has the same effect (`board_facts.py:92-99`). A concurrent story-plan read also hides that story's Ready tasks (`nextstep.py:642-648`). The new test covers two fixes with clean fake checks, so it passes in these broken cases.
findings.title: Not done: Close names a single merge when its report hides another Ready item

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - during an unsigned client prototype, the owner runs `forge merge enable` before sign-off while another fix is Ready. `repo.py:691-694` permits agent merges during the prototype, but `close.py:646-648` reserves the merge-enable fix for the owner. The reused report also collects human merge lines (`nextstep.py:386-391`), so close suggests `forge land <fix> let-the-agent-merge`. Following it starts a child land command that refuses the owner-only item (`land.py:64-69`), leaving the batch in Needs you. This contradicts the coordinator's rule that owner-held items are not named.
findings.title: Functional: Exclude the owner-held merge-enable fix from close's batch

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Scale
Case: normal use - closing any agent-merged item in a long-lived repo, including when it is the only Ready item, now builds the entire next report. With no supplied history, `nextstep.py:573-586` resolves every story individually; `nextstep.py:361-362` also rebuilds board statistics, whose `board.py:862-866` resolves the stories again. `story.py:902-911` launches Git history queries for their tasks. This repository already has 99 story records and 343 task records, so the added work grows with accumulated history and repeats on every successful close, including closes run by land.
findings.title: Scale: Avoid rebuilding the full next report after every successful close

why: Agents merge Ready items one at a time, so each merge after main moves costs a full CI run: forge close's Ready line says 'Next: forge merge <item>' even when other items are Ready, and the skill mentions the land train only in one table row; seen at a client on 19-20 Nov 2026
